mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved from -33.1 to -28.3 across the last two weekly means, and continued transit normalisation adds commuter footfall to retail corridors, so RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean of about -37.9.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.1 at t-2w to -28.3 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC stayed near -38
regime_hint: steady reopening with no new containment measures
failure_condition: TRANSIT keeps rising over the next 28 days but the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the last-28-day mean of -37.9.

mechanism_narrative: A crossing of the -30 level by TRANSIT marks a regime shift in which transit-dependent commercial catchments reopen; once TRANSIT prints above -30 for two consecutive weekly means, RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -30 (less than 30 percent below baseline) for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -28.3, the first weekly mean above -30 in the snapshot
regime_hint: reopening after transit capacity limits are eased
failure_condition: Within two weeks after TRANSIT prints above -30, RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its t-0w value of -37.7.

mechanism_narrative: The joint movement of RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES measures the home-to-work reallocation: when RESIDENTIAL drifts down while WORKPLACES rises, discretionary retail trips increase, pushing RETAIL_REC up over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls by at least 0.5 points versus the prior weekly mean while WORKPLACES weekly mean rises
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.9 at t-3w to 9.1 at t-0w while WORKPLACES rose from -31.1 to -29.1
regime_hint: gradual reopening with voluntary return to workplaces
failure_condition: The RESIDENTIAL-minus-WORKPLACES spread narrows over the next two weeks yet the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Winter policy stringency is proxied by RESIDENTIAL holding at or above +9: a persistent stay-at-home margin keeps discretionary trips suppressed, so RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days stays below its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays at or above +9 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has stayed between +9.1 and +9.9 for all four weekly means
regime_hint: tightening winter containment with stay-at-home persistence
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL holds at or above +9 for two more weekly means and the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC still exceeds the last-28-day mean of -37.9.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined monotonically from -12.0 to -14.6, showing households are collapsing the number of separate weekly errands; fewer total trip chains mean fewer spillover stops at retail, so RETAIL_REC weakens over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from -12.0 at t-3w to -14.6 at t-0w, the steepest four-week decline among the six series
regime_hint: steady state with reduced routine trip generation
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than the last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM continues to print at or below -14.

mechanism_narrative: Winter cold collapses park visits: PARKS rebounded 14.2 points from t-2w to t-1w and then dropped 3.9 points to -47.3. Each week-on-week parks decline displaces outdoor leisure time into indoor commercial venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls by at least 3 points versus the prior weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 3.9 points from -43.4 at t-1w to -47.3 at t-0w after a 14.2-point rebound
regime_hint: winter season with outdoor-to-indoor leisure substitution
failure_condition: After a week-on-week PARKS decline of at least 3 points, RETAIL_REC one week later is not above its value in the week of the parks decline.

mechanism_narrative: The reopening impulse is being absorbed: TRANSIT gained 3.6 points between t-2w and t-0w while RETAIL_REC moved only 0.4 points. When the transit-to-retail gap widens this way, retail does not follow transit, and RETAIL_REC drifts lower over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points while RETAIL_REC changes by less than 1 point over the same two weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -33.1 at t-2w to -28.3 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC moved from -38.1 to -37.7
failure_condition: In the week after the transit-to-retail gap widens by at least 3 points, RETAIL_REC rises above its prior weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: The year-end holiday shopping window lifts December retail footfall when no new containment is imposed; with TRANSIT improving and RETAIL_REC flat near -38 for four weeks, holiday demand pushes the next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC has been flat between -38.1 and -37.7 for four consecutive weekly means entering the year-end window
regime_hint: year-end holiday shopping window with no new containment measures
failure_condition: In the year-end window with no new restrictions imposed, the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the last-28-day mean of -37.9.
